claim: DN3 cells displayed a relatively high level of Zfp335 mRNA expression compared to DN4, DP, CD4, CD8, NKT, and γδ T cells.
source: We found that DN3 cells displayed a relatively high level of Zfp335 mRNA expression (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1A comparing Zfp335 expression across different thymocyte subsets.

claim: Zfp335 protein had the highest expression in DN3 thymocytes.
source: Flow cytometry analysis also revealed that Zfp335 protein had the highest expression in DN3 thymocytes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data showing mean fluorescence intensity of Zfp335 in different thymocyte populations.

claim: Microarray data from ImmGen showed higher expression of Zfp335 specifically at the DN3a stage during T-cell development from ETP to CD4/CD8 SP.
source: Consistently, microarray data from ImmGen showed higher expression of Zfp335 specifically at the DN3a stage during T-cell development from ETP to CD4/CD8 SP (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Supported by publicly available microarray data from the ImmGen database.

claim: RNA-seq data from ImmGen exhibited the highest expression of Zfp335 in DP thymocytes, with a gradually increased expression from ETP to DN3.
source: Although RNA-seq data from ImmGen exhibited the highest expression of Zfp335 in DP thymocytes, a gradually increased expression was observed from ETP to DN3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by publicly available RNA-seq data from the ImmGen database.

claim: LckCre+Zfp335fl/fl (KO) mice exhibited significantly smaller thymi and drastically decreased thymocyte numbers than WT control.
source: Strikingly, LckCre+Zfp335fl/fl (KO) mice exhibited significantly smaller thymi and drastically decreased thymocyte numbers than WT control (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by measurements of thymus size and total thymocyte counts shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Both percentages and numbers of DP cells, as well as CD4 SP and CD8 SP cells, were considerably reduced in KO mice.
source: Further analysis showed that both percentages and numbers of DP cells, as well as CD4 SP and CD8 SP cells, were considerably reduced in KO mice (Figure 1C–E).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data showing percentages and absolute numbers of different thymocyte populations.

claim: The percentage of DN cells was increased by nearly 10–15-folds in KO mice, although the total number was decreased.
source: Conversely, the percentage of DN cells was increased by nearly 10–15-folds, although the total number was decreased (Figure 1C–E).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data showing DN cell percentages and numbers.

claim: Reduced CD4+ and CD8+ cells were observed in the spleen and lymph nodes of KO mice.
source: In secondary lymphoid organs, we also observed reduced CD4+ and CD8+ cells in the spleen and lymph nodes (Figure 1F–J).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry analysis of peripheral lymphoid organs.

claim: Zfp335 is essential for the development of αβT cells in the thymus.
source: Thus, Zfp335 is essential for the development of αβT cells in the thymus.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the observed developmental defects in Zfp335-deficient mice.

claim: KO group produced fewer DP cells than WT control on both days 2 and 4 in OP9-DL1 coculture.
source: On both days 2 and 4, KO group produced fewer DP cells than WT control (Figure 2B–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by in vitro OP9-DL1 coculture experiments measuring DP cell generation.

claim: When DN3 cells from WT and KO mice were mixed and cocultured at a 1:4 ratio, significantly lower percentage and cell proportion of DP cells were observed in KO group.
source: When DN3 cells from WT (CD45.1+) and KO (CD45.2+) mice were mixed and cocultured at a 1:4 ratio (KO cells were rapidly competed out when used at a 1:1 ratio), significantly lower percentage and cell proportion of DP cells were also observed in KO group (Figure 2E–G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by mixed coculture experiments with congenic markers.

claim: Both the percentages and cell numbers of DP, CD4, and CD8 cells were significantly reduced while DN percentage was increased in mice that received KO bone marrow cells 6 weeks post transfer.
source: When thymocytes were analyzed 6 weeks post transfer, both the percentages and cell numbers of DP, CD4, and CD8 cells were significantly reduced while DN percentage was increased in the mice that received KO cells (Figure 2I, J, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by bone marrow chimera experiments analyzing thymocyte development in vivo.

claim: When WT and KO bone marrow cells were mixed at a 1:4 ratio for cotransfer experiments, fewer DP cell proportion was detected in KO compared to WT group.
source: Consistently, when WT and KO bone marrow cells were mixed at a 1:4 ratio for cotransfer experiments, fewer DP cell proportion detected in KO compared to WT group (Figure 2K, L; Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by mixed bone marrow chimera experiments.

claim: DN3 cells from KO mice generated fewer γδ T cells, despite a higher percentage, in comparison to WT controls after culturing for 4 days.
source: In addition, DN3 cells from KO mice also generated fewer γδ T cells, despite a higher percentage, in comparison to WT controls after culturing for 4 days (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by in vitro differentiation assays measuring γδ T cell generation.

claim: Zfp335 intrinsically regulates thymocyte development from DN to DP stage.
source: Together, we demonstrate that Zfp335 intrinsically regulates thymocyte development from DN to DP stage.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from multiple in vitro and in vivo experiments showing cell-intrinsic defects.

claim: A higher percentage of CD44−CD25+ DN3 cells but a lower percentage of CD44−CD25− DN4 cells were found in KO group compared to WT group.
source: The results showed that a higher percentage of CD44−CD25+ DN3 cells but a lower percentage of CD44−CD25− DN4 cells were found in KO group compared to WT group (Figure 3A, B), in which the numbers of both DN3 and DN4 thymocytes were decreased (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry analysis of DN thymocyte subsets.

claim: The numbers of both DN3 and DN4 thymocytes were decreased in KO mice.
source: The results showed that a higher percentage of CD44−CD25+ DN3 cells but a lower percentage of CD44−CD25− DN4 cells were found in KO group compared to WT group (Figure 3A, B), in which the numbers of both DN3 and DN4 thymocytes were decreased (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by absolute cell counts of DN3 and DN4 populations.

claim: The developmental blockade from DN3 to DN4 in Zfp335-deficient cells was verified by in vitro coculture assays on day 2 using OP9-DL1.
source: The developmental blockade from DN3 to DN4 in Zfp335-deficient cells was verified by in vitro coculture assays on day 2 using OP9-DL1 cultured with WT and KO DN3 cells, respectively (Figure 3D, E) or mixed at a 1:4 ratio (Figure 3F, G) as described above.
evidence: Supported by in vitro OP9-DL1 coculture experiments measuring DN3 to DN4 transition.

claim: The in vivo bone marrow chimera models confirmed the development block at the DN3 stage.
source: The in vivo bone marrow chimera models further confirmed the development block at the DN3 stage (Figure 3H–K), indicating that Zfp335 is indispensable for DN3 to DN4 transition during early-stage differentiation.
evidence: Supported by bone marrow chimera experiments showing DN3/DN4 ratios.

claim: Zfp335 is indispensable for DN3 to DN4 transition during early-stage differentiation.
source: The in vivo bone marrow chimera models further confirmed the development block at the DN3 stage (Figure 3H–K), indicating that Zfp335 is indispensable for DN3 to DN4 transition during early-stage differentiation.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from multiple experimental approaches showing DN3 to DN4 blockade.

claim: The in vivo BrdU incorporation assay showed comparable or even higher percentages of BrdU+ DN3 and DN4 cells in KO mice.
source: The in vivo BrdU incorporation assay showed comparable or even higher percentages of BrdU+ DN3 and DN4 cells (Figure 4A, B) as well as Ki67+ DN3 and DN4 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by BrdU incorporation and Ki67 staining experiments measuring cell proliferation.

claim: KO mice showed a remarkably higher percentages of Annexin V+ DN3 and DN4 cells compared to WT cells.
source: Nevertheless, when we examined thymocyte apoptosis, KO mice showed a remarkably higher percentages of Annexin V+ DN3 and DN4 cells compared to WT cells (Figure 4C, D).
evidence: Supported by Annexin V staining measuring apoptosis in DN thymocytes.

claim: After coculture with OP9-DL1 for 4 days, both Zfp335-deficient DN3 and DN4 cells showed an increased percentage of Annexin V+ cells.
source: After coculture with OP9-DL1 for 4 days, both Zfp335-deficient DN3 and DN4 cells showed an increased percentage of Annexin V+ cells (Figure 4E, F).
evidence: Supported by in vitro apoptosis assays in OP9-DL1 coculture system.

claim: The frequencies of both DN3a and DN3b were comparable between WT and Zfp335-deficient groups.
source: Further examination of the transition between the DN3a and DN3b stages found that the frequencies of both DN3a and DN3b were comparable between WT and Zfp335-deficient groups (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry analysis of DN3a and DN3b subpopulations.

claim: Both DN3a and DN3b cell populations showed enhanced cell apoptosis in Zfp335-deficient cells.
source: However, both cell populations showed enhanced cell apoptosis in Zfp335-deficient cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D–F), indicating that Zfp335 regulates thymocyte apoptosis in a TCR-independent manner.
evidence: Supported by Annexin V staining of DN3a and DN3b subsets.

claim: Zfp335 regulates thymocyte apoptosis in a TCR-independent manner.
source: However, both cell populations showed enhanced cell apoptosis in Zfp335-deficient cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2D–F), indicating that Zfp335 regulates thymocyte apoptosis in a TCR-independent manner.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that both pre- and post-β-selection DN3 cells show increased apoptosis.

claim: In mixed bone marrow chimeras, Zfp335-deficient DN3 and DN4 cells displayed significantly higher Annexin V+ cells.
source: Moreover, in mixed bone marrow chimeras, Zfp335-deficient DN3 and DN4 cells also displayed significantly higher Annexin V+ cells (Figure 4G, H), indicating an intrinsic role of Zfp355 in regulating thymocyte survival.
evidence: Supported by apoptosis analysis in mixed bone marrow chimeras.

claim: Zfp335 has an intrinsic role in regulating thymocyte survival.
source: Moreover, in mixed bone marrow chimeras, Zfp335-deficient DN3 and DN4 cells also displayed significantly higher Annexin V+ cells (Figure 4G, H), indicating an intrinsic role of Zfp355 in regulating thymocyte survival.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from competitive bone marrow chimera experiments.

claim: The expression of Ptcra (encoding pTα) was slightly increased in Zfp335-deficient DN3 and DN4 cells.
source: The expression of Ptcra (encoding pTα) was slightly increased while Trbc1, Trbc2, and Cd3e in DN3 and DN4 cells were comparable in WT and KO group (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Supported by qPCR analysis of pre-TCR component genes.

claim: Trbc1, Trbc2, and Cd3e expression in DN3 and DN4 cells were comparable in WT and KO group.
source: The expression of Ptcra (encoding pTα) was slightly increased while Trbc1, Trbc2, and Cd3e in DN3 and DN4 cells were comparable in WT and KO group (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: Supported by qPCR analysis of pre-TCR component genes.

claim: The expression of intracellular CD3 (iCD3) was unaffected in both Zfp335-deficient DN3 and DN4 cells.
source: Additionally, the expression of intracellular CD3 (iCD3) was also unaffected in both Zfp335-deficient DN3 and DN4 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A, B).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry analysis of intracellular CD3 expression.

claim: Flow cytometry analysis showed no substantial difference in iTCRβ expression between WT and KO DN3 cells.
source: Interestingly, flow cytometry analysis showed no substantial difference in iTCRβ expression between WT and KO DN3 cells, whereas Zfp335-deficient mice displayed a significant decrease in the percentage of iTCRβ+ DN4 cells (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry analysis of intracellular TCRβ expression.

claim: Zfp335-deficient mice displayed a significant decrease in the percentage of iTCRβ+ DN4 cells.
source: Interestingly, flow cytometry analysis showed no substantial difference in iTCRβ expression between WT and KO DN3 cells, whereas Zfp335-deficient mice displayed a significant decrease in the percentage of iTCRβ+ DN4 cells (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry analysis of intracellular TCRβ expression in DN4 cells.

claim: The expression of TCR Vβ5, Vβ6, Vβ8, and Vβ12 were decreased concomitantly in KO DN4 cells.
source: To further address whether Zfp335 deficiency affects TCRβ expression, we compared differential usage of TCRβ in DN4 cells between WT and KO mice, in which the expression of TCR Vβ5, Vβ6, Vβ8, and Vβ12 were decreased concomitantly (Figure 5C–F).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry analysis of different TCR Vβ chain usage.

claim: Genomic DNA analysis for V-DJβ5 and V-DJβ8 rearrangements showed no difference between WT and KO DN3 cells.
source: However, genomic DNA analysis for V-DJβ5 and V-DJβ8 rearrangements showed no difference between WT and KO DN3 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by PCR analysis of TCRβ gene rearrangements.

claim: The reduced iTCRβ expression may be a consequence of protein degradation.
source: Thus, the reduced iTCRβ expression may be a consequence of protein degradation.
evidence: Inferred from normal gene rearrangement but reduced protein expression.

claim: Forced expression of αβTCR successfully restored the decreased percentage of iTCRβ+ DN4 cells in the KO mice.
source: Notably, forced expression of αβTCR successfully restored the decreased percentage of iTCRβ+ DN4 cells in the KO mice, despite with little impact on the number of iTCRβ+ DN4 cells (Figure 5G–I).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry analysis of OT1 transgenic rescue experiments.

claim: Developmental arrest at the DN3 stage in Zfp335-deficient mice was fully rescued by OT1 transgene.
source: Importantly, developmental arrest at the DN3 stage in Zfp335-deficient mice was fully rescued by OT1 transgene (Figure 5J–L).
evidence: Supported by analysis of DN3/DN4 ratios in OT1 transgenic rescue experiments.

claim: DN3 and DN4 cells from OT1Tg KO mice still exhibited a similar degree of apoptosis with Zfp335-deficient cells.
source: Unfortunately, DN3 and DN4 cells from OT1Tg KO mice still exhibited a similar degree of apoptosis with Zfp335-deficient cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 4), suggesting Zfp335 affects thymocyte apoptosis in a TCR-independent manner.
evidence: Supported by Annexin V staining in OT1 transgenic rescue experiments.

claim: Zfp335 affects thymocyte apoptosis in a TCR-independent manner.
source: Unfortunately, DN3 and DN4 cells from OT1Tg KO mice still exhibited a similar degree of apoptosis with Zfp335-deficient cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 4), suggesting Zfp335 affects thymocyte apoptosis in a TCR-independent manner.
evidence: Inferred from persistent apoptosis despite TCR rescue.

claim: The proportions of DN, DP, CD4, and CD8 were still comparable in KO and OT1Tg KO mice.
source: Consistently, the proportions of DN, DP, CD4, and CD8 were still comparable in KO and OT1Tg KO mice (Figure 5M, N; Figure 5—figure supplement 5), demonstrating that the aberrant DP development has not yet been restored by αβTCR overexpression.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry analysis of thymocyte populations in OT1 transgenic mice.

claim: The aberrant DP development has not been restored by αβTCR overexpression.
source: Consistently, the proportions of DN, DP, CD4, and CD8 were still comparable in KO and OT1Tg KO mice (Figure 5M, N; Figure 5—figure supplement 5), demonstrating that the aberrant DP development has not yet been restored by αβTCR overexpression.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from persistent DP defects despite TCR rescue.

claim: Zfp335-deficient DN4 cells had a total 566 downregulated and 899 upregulated genes (fold change >1.25, p < 0.05).
source: Volcano plot showed that Zfp335-deficient DN4 cells had a total 566 downregulated and 899 upregulated genes (fold change >1.25, p < 0.05) (Figure 6A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq analysis comparing WT and KO DN4 cells.

claim: Gene ontology (GO) analysis highlighted a large fraction of genes downregulated in KO group belonging to lymphocyte differentiation and apoptotic pathways.
source: Gene ontology (GO) analysis highlighted a large fraction of genes downregulated in KO group belonging to lymphocyte differentiation and apoptotic pathways (Figure 6B).
evidence: Supported by GO enrichment analysis of RNA-seq data.

claim: A total of 2797 Zfp335-binding sites were identified by ChIP-seq.
source: To further determine genes directly regulated by Zfp335, we analyzed Zfp335 by chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by deep sequencing (ChIP-seq). We screened a total of 2797 Zfp335-binding sites (Supplementary file 2) and the prevalence of binding peaks across genomic regions was displayed as a pie chart (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-seq analysis of Zfp335 binding in DN thymocytes.

claim: 22 genes were overlapped between profoundly downregulated genes (twofold change cutoff) and Zfp335-targeting genes from ChIP-seq data.
source: To identify the Zfp335-targeting candidates, 119 profoundly downregulated genes were further selected out by a cutoff of twofold change, and 22 genes were overlapped with Zfp335-targeting genes from ChIP-seq data (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: Supported by integration of RNA-seq and ChIP-seq datasets.

claim: Bcl6 and Rorc were significantly downregulated in KO DN4 cells.
source: In line with RNA-seq results (Figure 6C), qPCR analysis verified that Bcl6 and Rorc were significantly downregulated in KO DN4 cells (Figure 6D).
evidence: Supported by both RNA-seq and qPCR validation.

claim: Zfp335 directly targeted the promoter regions of Bcl6 and Rorc in ChIP-seq analysis.
source: Importantly, Zfp335 directly targeted the promoter regions of Bcl6 and Rorc in ChIP-seq analysis (Figure 6E), which were further verified by luciferase assay (Figure 6F).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-seq showing Zfp335 binding peaks at Bcl6 and Rorc loci.

claim: Zfp335 binding to Bcl6 and Rorc promoters was verified by luciferase assay.
source: Importantly, Zfp335 directly targeted the promoter regions of Bcl6 and Rorc in ChIP-seq analysis (Figure 6E), which were further verified by luciferase assay (Figure 6F).
evidence: Supported by luciferase reporter assays showing transcriptional activation.

claim: Zfp335 directly regulates the transcription of Bcl6 and Rorc.
source: Taken together, in depth genomic analysis of DN thymocytes supports that Zfp335 directly regulates the transcription of Bcl6 and Rorc.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from combined ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, and luciferase assay data.

claim: Overexpression of Bcl6 and Rorc resulted in a substantial DP generation in KO DN3 cells cocultured with OP9-DL1.
source: After 3.5 days, overexpression of Bcl6 and Rorc resulted in a substantial DP generation, particularly in the Bcl6 group, resulting in a similar DP proportion to that in Zfp335-overexpressing cells (Figure 7B, C).
evidence: Supported by retroviral overexpression experiments in OP9-DL1 coculture.

claim: Overexpression of Psmg2, Dctn1, Ankle2, Cep76, Fgf13, and Ddx31 in KO DN3 cells did not restore DP generation in vitro.
source: Of note, overexpression of Psmg2, Dctn1, Ankle2, Cep76, Fgf13, and Ddx31 identified in the qPCR results (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B, C) in KO DN3 cells did not restore DP generation in vitro (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by retroviral overexpression experiments showing no rescue.

claim: Enhanced expression of Bcl6 in DN3 cells rescued DN thymocyte apoptosis.
source: Importantly, enhanced expression of Bcl6 in DN3 cells rescued DN thymocyte apoptosis (Figure 7D, E), while overexpression of both Bcl6 and Rorc rescued DP thymocytes from enhanced apoptosis (Figure 7F, G).
evidence: Supported by Annexin V staining in Bcl6 overexpression experiments.

claim: Overexpression of both Bcl6 and Rorc rescued DP thymocytes from enhanced apoptosis.
source: Importantly, enhanced expression of Bcl6 in DN3 cells rescued DN thymocyte apoptosis (Figure 7D, E), while overexpression of both Bcl6 and Rorc rescued DP thymocytes from enhanced apoptosis (Figure 7F, G).
evidence: Supported by Annexin V staining in Bcl6 and Rorc overexpression experiments.

claim: p53 is negatively regulated by Bcl6.
source: p53, negatively regulated by Bcl6, is involved in lymphocyte apoptosis (Haks et al., 1999; Guidos et al., 1996; Mombaerts et al., 1995).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Trp53 deletion resulted in a partial recovery of DP percentage, but not cell number, in Zfp335 KO mice.
source: Thus, we crossed Zfp335 KO strain with Trp53 KO strain to obtain double knockout mice, in which Trp53 deletion resulted in a partial recovery of DP percentage, but not cell number (Figure 7—figure supplement 2), further supporting the role of Bcl6 in Zfp335-controlled thymocyte survival.
evidence: Supported by analysis of double knockout mice.

claim: Zfp335 controls DN thymocyte survival through direct regulation of Bcl6 and Rorc expression.
source: Together, these data demonstrate that Zfp335 controls DN thymocyte survival through direct regulation of Bcl6 and Rorc expression.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from rescue experiments and genetic analysis.

claim: Zfp335 intrinsically controls DN to DP transition.
source: We demonstrate that Zfp335 intrinsically controls DN to DP transition, as T-cell-specific deficiency in Zfp335 leads to a substantial accumulation of DN3 along with reduction of DP, CD4+, and CD8+ thymocytes.
evidence: Summary statement based on multiple experimental findings.

claim: T-cell-specific deficiency in Zfp335 leads to a substantial accumulation of DN3 along with reduction of DP, CD4+, and CD8+ thymocytes.
source: We demonstrate that Zfp335 intrinsically controls DN to DP transition, as T-cell-specific deficiency in Zfp335 leads to a substantial accumulation of DN3 along with reduction of DP, CD4+, and CD8+ thymocytes.
evidence: Summary of phenotypic observations in Zfp335-deficient mice.

claim: The developmental blockade at DN stage results from the impaired intracellular TCRβ (iTCRβ) expression as well as increased susceptibility to apoptosis in thymocytes.
source: This developmental blockade at DN stage results from the impaired intracellular TCRβ (iTCRβ) expression as well as increased susceptibility to apoptosis in thymocytes.
evidence: Summary of mechanistic findings from multiple experiments.

claim: Enhanced expression of TCRβ restores the developmental defect during DN3 to DN4 transition.
source: Importantly, enhanced expression of TCRβ and Bcl6/Rorc restores the developmental defect during DN3 to DN4 transition and improves thymocytes survival, respectively.
evidence: Summary of rescue experiment results.

claim: Enhanced expression of Bcl6/Rorc improves thymocyte survival.
source: Importantly, enhanced expression of TCRβ and Bcl6/Rorc restores the developmental defect during DN3 to DN4 transition and improves thymocytes survival, respectively.
evidence: Summary of rescue experiment results.

claim: Zfp335 plays a critical role in controlling T-cell development by maintaining iTCRβ expression-mediated β-selection and independently activating cell survival signaling.
source: These findings identify a critical role of Zfp335 in controlling T-cell development by maintaining iTCRβ expression-mediated β-selection and independently activating cell survival signaling.
evidence: Overall conclusion summarizing the main findings of the study.

claim: Pre-TCR signals regulate thymocyte differentiation by mediating protection from apoptosis, stimulating proliferation, and inducing allelic exclusion at the TCRβ locus in post-β-selection DN3b cells and promoting DN to DP transition.
source: Pre-TCR signals regulate thymocyte differentiation by mediating protection from apoptosis, stimulating proliferation, and inducing allelic exclusion at the TCRβ locus in post-β-selection DN3b cells and promoting DN to DP transition (Hoffman et al., 1996; Aifantis et al., 1997; Kruisbeek et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Inactivation of pre-TCR components dampens T-lymphocyte development by arresting thymocytes at the DN3 stage and inducing apoptosis.
source: Inactivation of pre-TCR components dampens T-lymphocyte development by arresting thymocytes at the DN3 stage and inducing apoptosis (Fehling et al., 1995; Malissen et al., 1995; Mombaerts et al., 1992a; Mombaerts et al., 1992b).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Bcl6 induced by pre-TCR signals is involved in the DN to DP transition and protection of DN4 cells from apoptosis.
source: Apart from the essential role in the T follicular helper cell lineage commitment (Yu et al., 2009), Bcl6 induced by pre-TCR signals is also involved in the DN to DP transition and protection of DN4 cells from apoptosis (Solanki et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Abrogation of Rorc expression in thymocytes leads to a decreased DP proportion and impaired DP survival in a Bcl-xl-dependent manner.
source: Additionally, abrogation of Rorc expression in thymocytes leads to a decreased DP proportion and impaired DP survival in a Bcl-xl-dependent manner (Villey et al., 1999; Sun et al., 2000; Xi et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Germline knockout of Zfp335 is embryonic lethal.
source: Germline knockout of Zfp335 is embryonic lethal, while deletion of Zfp335 gene in nerve cells impairs the proliferation and differentiation of nerve progenitor cells in mice, eventually leading to severe microcephaly (Yang et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Deletion of Zfp335 gene in nerve cells impairs the proliferation and differentiation of nerve progenitor cells in mice, eventually leading to severe microcephaly.
source: Germline knockout of Zfp335 is embryonic lethal, while deletion of Zfp335 gene in nerve cells impairs the proliferation and differentiation of nerve progenitor cells in mice, eventually leading to severe microcephaly (Yang et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The Zfp335bloto allele, a missense mutation derived from ENU mutagenesis, does not significantly affect thymocyte development but causes a significant reduction in the number of peripheral T cells due to defects in the maturation and migration of thymocytes.
source: Function of Zfp335 in T-cell development has been observed in the study of the Zfp335bloto allele, a missense mutation derived from ENU mutagenesis. While thymocyte development is not significantly affected by this hypomorph mutation, there is a significant reduction in the number of peripheral T cells due to defects in the maturation and migration of thymocytes (Han et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Overexpression of neither Bcl6 nor Rorc in Zfp335-deficient DN3 thymocytes could restore the decreased iTCRβ expression.
source: Moreover, Zfp335 regulates TCRβ expression independent on Bcl6 and Rorc since overexpression of neither Bcl6 or Rorc in Zfp335-deficient DN3 thymocytes could restore the decreased iTCRβ expression (Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry analysis of iTCRβ expression in rescue experiments.

claim: Zfp335 regulates TCRβ expression independent of Bcl6 and Rorc.
source: Moreover, Zfp335 regulates TCRβ expression independent on Bcl6 and Rorc since overexpression of neither Bcl6 or Rorc in Zfp335-deficient DN3 thymocytes could restore the decreased iTCRβ expression (Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Inferred from failure of Bcl6/Rorc to rescue iTCRβ expression.
